subject: APAC edge routing: subprocessor attestation + TIA mapping request

From: Andrew Choe <andrew.choe@hearthcarelabs.com>

Cc: HearthCare Legal <legal@hearthcarelabs.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC pilot: TIA mapping and subprocessor attestation needed

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — HearthCare is excited to kick the APAC pilot (Japan + SG) in Q4. Before we can start ingesting real PHI-adjacent telemetry we need two things from Redwood Legal/Trust:

1) A short mapping that shows which Redwood subprocessors will process or transit APAC-resident personal data for this pilot (including edge accelerators, logging, monitoring, and backup targets).
2) A copy of the proposed TIA we can share with our compliance team (they asked specifically about UK IDTA language and fallback to SCCs where relevant).

We attached our standard checklist to show the gating items — main ask is an attestation for any new APAC edge providers and confirmation whether data will ever leave APAC for processing. Can you also confirm timeline if we need a vendor attestation (DocuSign)?

Attached: TIA-proposal-v0.9.pdf (draft)

Appreciate quick turnaround — HearthCare needs this to complete its vendor security board by 23 Sep.

Best,
Andrew
Head of Integrations, HearthCare Labs

Can we aim to get an initial registry + draft attestation out by EOD 17 Sep? If vendors need to sign attestation via DocuSign we can provision that but it slows the runbook by ~3 business days.

Attachments: subprocessor_registry_v3.csv (internal export)

-Markus

Markus / Andrew —

I pulled the current registry and attached the export (subprocessor_registry_v3.csv) and a short APAC PSA checklist for the pilot. Highlights:

- EdgeStream (Tokyo) — new edge CDN / inference edge partner we onboarded as a regional cache in June. They have ephemeral compute in JP region; they do not persist raw payloads beyond 24 hours (our config) but they do handle decrypted inference traffic for latency-sensitive routes.
- LogFast SG — logging pipeline; logs are forwarded to our central observability fleet but we can configure a geo-partitioned retention policy. Currently, some debug logs are routed through a US backup for DR.
- No other new APAC subprocessors.

Immediate asks for HearthCare:
1) Do you require vendor-level attestation signatures for each subprocessor? If so we will send DocuSign packets to EdgeStream and LogFast — time to signature typically 2–4 business days.
2) Naomi: please confirm if the UK IDTA wording is required for this APAC-only pilot (Andrew mentioned HearthCare legal likes global fallback).

Attaching: apac-psa-checklist.xlsx

-Kimberly

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Choe <andrew.choe@hearthcarelabs.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC pilot: TIA mapping and subprocessor attestation needed

Team / Andrew —

Reviewed the TIA-proposal-v0.9.pdf and Kimberly's registry notes. My read and proposed amendments:

- UK IDTA / Addendum: If HearthCare handles any UK personal data (even indirectly via multi-jurisdictional user base), we need to preserve the option of an UK IDTA addendum or at least an explicit fallback clause. For an APAC-only pilot you could accept SCCs for transfers that briefly transit EU/UK, but we must not offer a blanket exception.
- Subprocessor attestations: for EdgeStream (Tokyo) we require a scoped attestation that covers (1) no persistent storage of raw personal data beyond 24 hours, (2) controls for key material (HSM or equivalent), and (3) audit access within 30 days. LogFast needs to confirm geo-retention partitioning in writing.
- Retention & deletion: tighten retention language in §4.2 to include a 90-day max for debug logs containing IDs unless customer approves longer retention.

If vendors cannot sign the attestation we should implement technical mitigations (tokenize before edge, strip identifiers in logs). I will prepare a redline of the TIA with the above items and an explicit UK-IDTA fallback paragraph.

Timeline: I can get a redline by EOD 17 Sep and a final legal-approved TIA by COB 20 Sep provided vendor attestations arrive on schedule.

-Naomi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
